The app
What the user sees
Live numbers
Free bikes, free docks, occupancy, empty stations
History
Free bikes over 1 h, 6 h or 24 h, from stored snapshots
Station map
Every station, coloured by bikes left: 0, 1–3, 4+
Architecture
Five VMs, one job each
ui — nginx + React, Cloudflare tunnel
history — Flask API and poller
fetcher — calls the CityBikes API
db — PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, Loki, Grafana
bastion — the only SSH entry
One Dockerfile per service · Vagrant + VirtualBox
Data path
How one snapshot is made
01
History
The poller puts a request on the queue every minute
02
Queue
RabbitMQ or pgmq: request and reply share one id
03
Fetcher
Takes the request and calls the CityBikes API
04
Reply
All 60 stations go back through the queue
05
PostgreSQL
History stores the snapshot in one transaction
06
UI
The browser shows the new numbers and chart
Runtime switches
Swap the queue and the cache without a rebuild
Variable in .env
Default
Alternative
QUEUE_BACKEND
rabbitmq
postgres → pgmq
CACHE_BACKEND
redis
postgres → hstore
$ bash scripts/switch-backend.sh queue=postgres cache=postgres
Same images: only the containers are recreated with the new variable
Security
Only the website faces outside
Private network
10.20.0.0/24: the LAN sees only ui and bastion
Bastion
SSH keys only; other VMs only from the bastion
Cloudflare Tunnel
HTTPS domain, no public IP, no open ports
Secrets
Only in .env and mode-600 files, never in images
Containers
Non-root, cap-drop ALL, read-only, health checks
Least privilege
Each container gets only its own backend’s credentials
Observability
Logs from every VM in one place
Collect → store
Alloy on each VM ships container logs and the journal to Loki (7 days)
SSH tunnel in
Grafana is private: forward it through the bastion
ssh -L 3000:10.20.0.50:3000 bastion
Log in
localhost:3000 with Grafana credentials (admin + password from .env)

Conclusion
Three ideas behind the project
Decouple
Services talk only through a queue, and the queue itself can be swapped at runtime
One door in
Private network, bastion with keys, a public site with no open ports
See everything
Logs from all five VMs in one dashboard, behind a login
